identification: Unsigned 19th century brass drum-type pocket/field compound microscope in a fitted mahogany case with cotton wool and accessory compartments, plus a separate inlaid rosewood box (mother-of-pearl dots, purple silk lining) that looks like a writing or dressing box and is of little value. Photos show no maker name, no engraving and no objective or slide set. Looks complete but basic, likely English or continental c.1850-1900.

viewing_check: Open the case and check for any engraving or maker/retailer name on the drum, base or tailpiece (a named London maker lifts value a lot); count lenses/objectives and any slides or forceps; check the draw tube and focus move smoothly and the mirror and cap are present; check for lacquer loss, dents or replaced parts; confirm the inlaid box is sound (hinge, lock), as it adds little.
